title: Two runners, no notebook
hook: A chain may loop back. Can two markers tell?

knows: a linked list as boxes with arrows (insert-at-front-cost)
doesNotKnow: how to tell a looping list from a long one without remembering every box

misconception: To detect a loop you must remember every box you have visited.
objective: The learner can explain that inside a loop the fast marker gains exactly one box per tick, so the gap shrinks by one and cannot skip over zero, and that two markers and no memory of visited boxes are enough.

claims.text: On the 7-box chain whose last arrow goes back to box 3, slow is on boxes 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and fast on 3, 5, 7, 4, 6 at ticks 1 to 5, so they share box 6 at tick 5.
claims.source: Builder's node trace (scratchpad th.mjs), 2026-10-14: slow 2,3,4,5,6; fast 3,5,7,4,6. Fast goes 7 to 3 to 4 at tick 4.

claims.text: Your green arc, the boxes fast still had to run to reach slow, was 3, then 2, then 1, then they shared box 6 at tick 5.
claims.source: Builder's node trace: gap = (slow - fast) mod 5 over loop boxes 3 to 7 gives 3, 2, 1, 0 at ticks 2 to 5. | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): Same numbers (ticks 2-5: 3, 2, 1, 0), now phrased as the forward distance from fast to slow that the stage draws as an arc; r5 found 'behind' contradicted the picture (fast looked 2-3 boxes ahead). | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): own trace (scratchpad fc22/tort.mjs): gapOf() 3, 2, 1, 0 at ticks 2-5, equal to a forward walk count along the arrows from fast to slow; meet on box 6 at tick 5. Arc drawn only for gap > 0, so the arcs are 3, 2, 1.

claims.text: In a loop the fast one gains exactly one box per tick, so the arc shrinks by one box and cannot step over 0.
claims.source: Per tick fast moves 2 and slow moves 1, so the distance fast is behind along the loop changes by exactly 1. A gap that falls by 1 from a whole number reaches 0. | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): 'gap counts down' became 'the arc shrinks by one box' to point at the stage; the duplicated closing line 'The gap shrinks by one each tick, so it must hit zero' was removed. | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): both in the ring: ((s+1) - (f+2)) mod 5 = gap - 1, so the forward gap falls by exactly 1 per tick and reaches 0 without skipping.

claims.text: With the last arrow pointing nowhere, fast reaches box 7 at tick 3 and has no arrow to follow: no loop.
claims.source: Builder's node trace: without the 7 to 3 arrow, slow is on 2,3,4 and fast on 3,5,7 at ticks 1 to 3; box 7 has no next box.

claims.text: The two markers meet for every tail of 0 to 10 boxes and every loop of 1 to 10 boxes.
claims.source: Builder's node script over all 110 combinations: none failed to meet (the brief's loop of 5 is odd and still meets).

claims.text: This is Floyd's tortoise and hare, which keeps only two markers and no list of visited boxes.
claims.source: Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming Vol. 2, section 3.1, exercise 6, attributes cycle finding to Floyd. 'Two markers' is a derivation: the algorithm stores only two positions. · Fact-check pass 19 2026-10-14: VERIFIED. Floyd attribution corroborated by a secondary source citing Knuth TAOCP Vol. 2, p. 7, ex. 6 (Gammie, AFP TortoiseHare); one other secondary source numbers it ex. 7, so cite "section 3.1, exercises 6-7" if the number matters. Could not open Knuth itself.

claims.text: Stage readout: 'Gap n boxes fast must run to reach slow (green arc)', drawn as a green arc inside the ring from fast forward to slow; 'Gap —: slow not in the loop yet' before slow reaches box 3, and 'Gap —: no loop here' when the last arrow points nowhere.
claims.source: gapOf() in Demo.tsx: (slow - fast) mod 5 on the ring of boxes 3-7, i.e. the arrows fast must follow to reach slow; GapArc draws that many 72-degree steps from fast's box. Tick 2: slow 3, fast 5, arc 5→6→7→3 = 3. | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): new sentence. New stage text (r5 top finding: Gap was undefined on stage). | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Demo.tsx gapText/gapWhy render 'Gap n boxes fast must run to reach slow (green arc)', 'Gap —: slow not in the loop yet' (tick 1, slow on 2), 'Gap —: no loop here' when nowhere; GapArc steps 72° from fast's box in arrow order (angOf matches CENTRE).

recall.question: A linked list is 1,000 boxes long and may loop. You run a slow marker (1 box per tick) and a fast one (2 boxes per tick). If there is a loop inside, what does the fast marker's distance behind the slow one do once both are in it?
options: Shrinks by one each tick until they share a box
Grows, so you must remember visited boxes
recall.why: Fast gains one box per tick, so the gap counts down by one and cannot skip zero. No list of visited boxes is needed.
